$schema.description: The JSON Schema of the file: `./manifest.schema.json`.

manifestVersion.description: The version of the manifest format.

generatedAt.description: When the manifest was built, in ISO 8601.

version.description: The version of the root package.json.

commit.description: The commit the manifest was built from, or null outside git.

version.description: The version of the contract format.

idAttribute.description: The attribute that carries an anchor.

idPattern.description: The regular expression every rendered anchor matches.

additionalProperties.description: What an element of the kind is.
The part of a composite the suffix marks.

kind.description: The kind of the part: the last word of its suffix.

description.description: What the part is: the meaning of its suffix in the vocabulary.

additionalProperties.description: What the part says while it carries the value.

values.description: The data-value values the suffix itself defines, never rows of `choiceValues`.

additionalProperties.description: The part a derived suffix marks.

derivedParts.description: Each derived suffix with the part it marks: its kind, its meaning and, when the suffix defines them, its data-value values (a `visibility-button`: `show`, `hide`).

additionalProperties.description: `<on>: <meaning>`: the elements that carry it, then what it holds.

attributes.description: The attributes an anchored element or the page carries.

appStateAnchor.description: The anchor of the readiness line of the app.

propertyNames.description: A state of the vocabulary (data-state).

additionalProperties.description: What the state means.

appStates.description: The data-state values of the app.

readyValue.description: The app state in which a test may start.

propertyNames.description: A state of the vocabulary (data-state).

additionalProperties.description: What the state means.

containerStates.description: The data-state values of a list, a section or a page status.

propertyNames.description: A state of the vocabulary (data-state).

additionalProperties.description: `<where>: <meaning>`: the anchor that takes it, then what it means.

rowStates.description: The data-state values of an item.

propertyNames.description: A code of the vocabulary (data-code).

additionalProperties.description: `<where>: <meaning>`: the anchors that carry it, then what it means.

codes.description: The data-code values: what a message, error, toast or dialog says.

additionalProperties.description: What the value chooses.
The values the anchor carries.

choiceValues.description: The data-value values by anchor; a value that starts with `^` is a pattern of values.

propertyNames.description: A role of the vocabulary.

additionalProperties.description: Who acts in the role.

roles.description: The roles a device acts as.

propertyNames.description: A screen name of the vocabulary: one or two kebab-case segments.

additionalProperties.description: The screen and its route.

screenNames.description: The screen names an anchor starts with.

items.description: A declared anchor: 2 to 4 dot-separated kebab-case segments, kind last.

reserved.description: The anchors the shell owns; a feature never declares them.

additionalProperties.description: What the composite is for.

composites.description: The composites the platform declares once, derived into the screens whose field opts in; the declaration itself is under `platform.composites`.

pageHelper.description: Where development and e2e builds install the page helper on `window`.

readiness.description: When a page is ready for a test to act on it.

language.description: Which language the page speaks, and what to assert.

session.description: How a scenario starts and makes its accounts.

screenMap.description: How to read `screens` and the fields of an anchor.

bindings.description: Where each kind of binding points.

model.description: How to read `model` and its `x-perch` keyword.

notices.description: How to find the notice an action raises.

activities.description: How to read `activities`, the machines of visits to screens.

scenarios.description: How to read `scenarios` and their bracket references.

gaps.description: What to do when the contract cannot say what a build needs.

instructions.description: Prose instructions for an agent that drives the application.

contract.description: The vocabulary of the contract, with instructions for an agent.

id.description: A screen name of the vocabulary: one or two kebab-case segments.

title.description: The title of the screen, for a reader.

description.description: What the screen is for: the task it serves and when it is shown, in one or two sentences, so an agent chooses the screen before reading its anchors. Not a list of its parts: each anchor has a description of its own. At most 200 characters.

frame.description: The frame around every screen: it has no route of its own.

path.description: The route path: static segments, `$param`, `{-$param}` (optional) and `$` (splat), from `/`.

guard.description: Who may open the route: only a guest, or only a signed-in account; absent: anyone.

params.description: The path parameters, as a flat JSON Schema.

type.description: Always "object".
The primitive type of the parameter.

items.description: A string, number or boolean value.

default.description: The value when the URL leaves it out.

examples.description: Fake values of the parameter, each one it accepts; the first fills the example link.

minimum.description: The smallest value of a number or an integer.

maximum.description: The largest value of a number or an integer.

anyOf.description: Several bindings: the anchor runs them in this order, or one of them depending on the mode of the screen; the flow says which.

binding.description: What the anchor is bound to: one binding, or several in a non-empty list.

roles.description: The roles that see the element; absent: every role of the screen.

own.description: Shown to a member only on the entries the member owns.

holdsInput.description: A field holds input: what is typed into it stays until an action takes it, so a leave with it typed loses it. False for a field whose own change runs its action, which applies at once.

secret.description: A field that holds a secret (a password, its confirmation, a current password): it never leaves the page but in the request of the action that takes it, so no navigate carries it into a search and no search parameter starts it; only a secret input renders a `visibility-button`.

codes.description: The data-code values the element carries.

ranked.description: A message whose codes are in rank order: of the codes raised before it shows, it shows the first, and the others go with it; a clear of it, in any flow, takes away every code raised before it. Only a message of two codes or more, each once.

fields.description: An error's codes, each with the field of the screen it concerns, which the error shows under and marks invalid; a code left out concerns the form.

propertyNames.description: A code of the vocabulary (data-code).

additionalProperties.description: A declared anchor: 2 to 4 dot-separated kebab-case segments, kind last.

dataId.description: What the data-id of the element holds: the id of the entity it shows.

dataValue.description: The element carries a data-value from the choice values.

states.description: The data-state values the element takes.

derived.description: The derived suffixes the element renders: `confirm-button`, `option`; an `input` alone renders `visibility-button`, the eye of a password input.

entity.description: The entity of model.schema.json the anchor lists.

order.description: The field the entries are ordered by.

anyOf.description: The entries come from an entity of the model.

platform.description: The platform action whose result the anchor lists.

anyOf.description: The entries come from a platform action.

source.description: Where the entries of a list, a section or a table come from.

code.description: The code it asks with: what the action destroys.

asks.description: Derived: the control asks the frame's confirmation before its action runs, the action being destructive (a delete of the model; a delete, remove or revoke of the platform).

composite.description: The platform composite the field opts into (`password-rules`): the loader derives its list and items on the screen, `<screen>.<list>` and `<screen>.<list>.<item>-item`; only a secret input opts in.
The composite that derives the anchor.

item.description: The item of the composite the anchor stands for; absent: the list.

derivedFrom.description: Derived: the anchor is the list, or one item, of a platform composite a field of the screen opted into; a screen file never writes it.

additionalProperties.description: One declared anchor.

states.description: The container states of the screen, each with what is visible in it.

additionalProperties.description: What is visible on the screen in this container state; the vocabulary says what the state means, and each anchor what it is for in a description of its own. At most 200 characters.

id.description: The id of the machine: a one-segment name the flow declares, which the app gives its machine, and an id target `#<id>.<state>` names (one segment, as XState splits a target on `.`); absent, the app names the machine by the screen id.

description.description: What the flow does as a whole that no single state says: how its areas or its modes go together. Its states, events, guards and effects say the rest. At most 200 characters.

initial.description: The state the screen opens in.

meta.description: What the contract says of the flow beyond XState: its guards.

guards.description: The guards by name, each with what it holds: a sentence, or `{ codes }`, the failure codes it holds for.

propertyNames.description: A guard: a camelCase name of the flow `meta.guards`.

anyOf.description: What the guard holds, in one sentence the app implements; a guard that tells the failures of an action apart takes their codes, `{ codes }`, instead. At most 200 characters.

codes.description: The codes it holds for: the action failed with one of them.

anyOf.description: A guard by failure code, on a branch of an `onError` only: it holds when the action failed with one of its codes.

propertyNames.description: A state of the flow, a key of its `states`: `sign-in`, `signing-in`.

description.description: What a tester or a user tells apart in the state that its events, effects and `meta.renders` do not say. At most 200 characters.

type.description: The flow ends in this state.

meta.description: What the contract says of the state beyond XState: its address and the anchors it renders.

address.description: The route that reaches this state: a link or a reload restores it.

renders.description: Anchors of the screen that only some states render, this one among them: an anchor no state of the flow lists is rendered in every state, one that a state lists only in the states that list it, and the anchors declared under it (`<anchor>.<rest>`) with it; a state of a region also renders what its parallel state lists.

language.description: Where the mail's language comes from: a parameter of the action that holds one of the app's languages; `account`: the settings of the account the action acts on once it has them, else the language it signed up in; or `recipient`: the account whose email the mail goes to, read the same way, else the signed-in account's.

screen.description: The screen the link opens, at the path of its route.

search.description: The search parameter of that screen's route the link carries its token in.

notices.description: The notices the action sends, when it sends any: mails that only tell, with no token, each by its name.

name.description: The name of the notice, unique within the action: `password-changed`; a scenario names it `[notice:<action>.<name>]`.

to.description: The parameter of the action whose value the notice goes to, or `account`: the email of the account the action acts on, as it was before the action changed anything (an email changed is told to the old address).

language.description: Where the mail's language comes from: a parameter of the action that holds one of the app's languages, or `account`: the settings of the account the action acts on once it has them, else the language it signed up in.

link.description: The plain link of the notice, when it has one: a password changed links to the reset of a password, if it was not the account's owner.

screen.description: The screen the link opens, at a route that needs no parameter: the link carries no token and no search.

items.description: A notice the action sends: a mail that only tells, with no token.

additionalProperties.description: One platform action.

actions.description: The platform actions by name: `platform.<name>` in a binding.

events.description: The events the platform raises, by name, each with what it means: `platform.<name>` as an event of a flow.

additionalProperties.description: What the event means: when the platform raises it. What follows is said by the flows that handle it. At most 200 characters.

leaving.description: The actions whose run leaves what the user typed behind (a sign-out, a switch of organisation, a change of language), as a binding names them: the app is to ask before one runs while a field holds unsaved input.

items.description: `entity.action` (an action of the entity x-perch) or `platform.<name>` (an action of platform.actions).

toasts.description: The platform actions whose success toasts, each with the code of its toast (`organisations.create: organisation-created`): an invoke of a listed action gets the standard toast, as an action of the model does; an unlisted platform action never toasts.

propertyNames.description: A platform action: `sign-in`, `organisations.create`.

additionalProperties.description: A code of the vocabulary (data-code).

composites.description: The composites by name: a list with its items the platform declares once (`password-rules`), derived into every screen whose secret input writes `composite: <name>`.

description.description: What the composite is for: the list it derives on a screen carries it, and each item has a description of its own. At most 200 characters.

list.description: The last segment of the list the composite derives on a screen, `<screen>.<list>`: a `list`, so it ends with `-list` (`password-rule-list`).

itemState.description: The data-state each item takes once what it says holds: a row state of the vocabulary (`met`).

additionalProperties.description: What the item of the composite's list says: every screen that opts in derives an item anchor with it as its description, and the composite's `itemState` marks it. At most 200 characters.

items.description: The items by name, each with its description: the screen gets `<screen>.<list>.<name>-item`, an `item` with the item state.

additionalProperties.description: A composite the platform declares once where its policy lives: a list with its items, derived into every screen whose field opts in with `composite: <name>`.

question.description: The reserved dialog that asks in the app whether to leave and lose what was typed: its code names what it asks, its confirm-button leaves, its cancel-button stays.

screen.description: A change of screen the user starts: a link, Back, Forward.

actions.description: A control bound to an action of `leaving`, before the action runs.

unload.description: A reload, closing the tab or the window, an address typed by hand: the browser's own prompt, drawn outside the page, so no anchor or code marks it.

state.description: A change of state inside one screen: a tab, a search parameter, a form opened or closed.

flow.description: A navigation a flow makes after its action completed: the action took the input.

elsewhere.description: A leave nobody started here: another tab or device signed the account in or out, a database that will not open. Nothing here can keep what was typed.

unsavedInput.description: Every leave that would lose what the user typed and did not save, and how the app asks first: through the question, by the browser, never, or it cannot.

items.description: A declared anchor: 2 to 4 dot-separated kebab-case segments, kind last.

reserved.description: The anchors the shell owns; a feature never declares them.

anchor.description: The anchor of the readiness line of the app.

states.description: The app states it takes, in order.

status.description: The readiness line of the app.

platform.description: What the platform offers every screen.

id.description: The id of the activity, the name of its file: `session`.

title.description: The title of the activity, for a reader.

description.description: What the activity is for: the task it serves across its screens. Its states are the visits, and the screens do the work. At most 200 characters.

roles.description: The roles that take part in the activity.

data.description: What the activity carries from screen to screen, by name.

propertyNames.description: A name of what the activity carries: one or two kebab-case segments.

description.description: What the activity carries from screen to screen; `model` names the field of the model it is. At most 200 characters.

model.description: `entity.field`: a field of an entity of model.schema.json.

initial.description: The state the activity starts in.

meta.description: What the contract says of the machine beyond XState: its guards.

guards.description: The guards by name, each with what it holds.

propertyNames.description: A guard: a camelCase name of the flow `meta.guards`.

propertyNames.description: A state of the activity, a key of its `states`: a visit to a screen, `sign-in`, `signed-out`.

type.description: The activity ends in this state.

screen.description: The screen the state is a visit to: a screen id.

path.description: The path of a binding of that screen.

address.description: The route of the visit: the activity is where its address is.

meta.description: What the contract says of the state beyond XState: its screen and address.

on.description: Per anchor of the state's screen or of the frame, where acting on it leads.

propertyNames.description: An anchor (a data-testid): 2 to 5 dot-separated kebab-case segments.

target.description: The state the activity moves to: the next visit.

guard.description: A guard: a camelCase name of the flow `meta.guards`.

description.description: What acting on the anchor leads to that the target and the guard do not say; the flows of the screens do the work. At most 200 characters.

anyOf.description: One transition: the user acts on the anchor and reaches the target.

guard.description: A guard: a camelCase name of the flow `meta.guards`.

description.description: What acting on the anchor leads to that the target and the guard do not say; the flows of the screens do the work. At most 200 characters.

items.description: One transition: the user acts on the anchor and reaches the target.

anyOf.description: Guarded transitions in order: the first whose guard holds is taken.
